title: The Three Layers of Software Assurance
description: Interactive p5.js concentric-circle infographic of the three layers of software assurance: In-Code Defenses at the center, Analysis Tooling in the middle ring, and Supply Chain controls in the outer ring. Hover any chip for its definition; hover a ring for what that layer protects against.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

educational.topic: Software assurance: in-code defenses, analysis tooling, and supply-chain controls
learningObjectives: Explain how in-code defenses, analysis tooling, and supply-chain controls compose to defend a software system.
Match a specific control (e.g., parameterized queries, SAST, SBOM) to its assurance layer.
Articulate which layer fails when a particular incident occurs.
educational.prerequisites: Awareness that software has vulnerabilities and uses third-party dependencies.

pedagogical.modelType: static concentric-layer infographic with hover reveals
controls: Hover a chip: show its one-line definition
Hover a ring: update the 'what this layer protects against' caption
pedagogical.assessment: Given an incident (SQL injection succeeded, a vulnerable dependency was shipped, a build server was compromised), students name which layer should have caught it.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing one layer (e.g., a scanner) is sufficient on its own.
Treating supply-chain risk as separate from software assurance rather than its outermost layer.
